events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
ESFRIW

A wet weather system will support periods of showers and
thunderstorms across Wyoming Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. This
weather system is funneling abundant tropical moisture into the
state. Given this anomalously high moisture, many thunderstorms will
feature heavy rainfall, possibly leading to localized flooding. Poor
drainage areas, urban areas, and steep terrain will be the most
susceptible locations for this isolated flooding.

Many locations could see rainfall totals anywhere between 0.75" to
1.75" through Sunday afternoon, with a majority of this rain falling
quickly in thunderstorms.

Remember, if you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around don't down!

events.summary:
At 1003 AM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking strong thunderstorms along
a line extending from 11 miles northwest of Utah Test and Training
Range North to 9 miles northwest of Knolls. Movement was northeast at
35 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Knolls, Utah Test and Training Range North, and Lakeside.

This includes Interstate 80 in Utah between mile markers 28 and 67.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...East Central Palm Beach County in southeastern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 200 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1201 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Wellington, Greenacres, Royal Palm Beach, Haverhill, Golden
Lakes, Lake Belvedere Estates, Royal Palm Estates, Florida
Gardens, Aberdeen Golf Course, Aberdeen, Plantation Mobile Home
Park, Stacey Street and Century Village.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of Iowa, including the following counties,
Allamakee, Howard, Mitchell and Winneshiek, southeast Minnesota,
including the following counties, Dodge, Fillmore, Houston, Mower,
Olmsted and Winona, and Wisconsin, including the following
counties, Crawford, Grant, La Crosse, Monroe, Richland and Vernon.

* WHEN...From 7 PM CDT this evening through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding
may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Widespread rain has developed across the region today and will
continue into the day Saturday. The heaviest rainfall will occur
from Friday evening through Saturday morning. Some locations may
see multiple inches of rainfall, particularly near and south of
Interstate 94.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southwestern Lincoln County in central New Mexico...
Southeastern Socorro County in central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 957 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated moderate rain and
Meteorologists reported water over roads and washed out dirt
roads near and south of US Highway 380 across far southeast
Socorro County and far southwest Lincoln County. This is causing
arroyo and small stream flooding. Between 0.25 and 0.75 inches of
rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.25 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Oscuro.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
